method.method_draft: First read the graph visually: the horizontal axis is HOURS and the vertical axis is MILES. The plotted ride starts at the origin, 0 hours and 0 miles, and its final plotted point is at 7 hours and 35 miles. From the question text, identify that it asks for average speed over the entire ride in miles per hour. Use the rule average speed = total miles traveled ÷ total time elapsed, so compute 35 ÷ 7 = 5 mph.

method.method_draft: First read the graph visually as a piecewise distance-time graph with key points approximately at (0,0), (1,5), (2,15), (4,20), and (7,35). From the text, note that the graph gives miles traveled during the ride and asks for the entire-ride average speed. Compute the distance gained on each segment: 5, 10, 5, and 15 miles, totaling 35 miles. Compute the time spent on each segment: 1, 1, 2, and 3 hours, totaling 7 hours. Then average speed for the whole ride is total segment distances divided by total segment times: 35 ÷ 7 = 5 mph.
